$comment: Observation layouts the Q1 motion-control runtime expects. Transcribed from
Every field index is a half-open slice [start, start+size) into the flat obs vector.
Joint-ordered fields use robots/q1/contract/joints.yaml order, indices 0..21.

mimic_opensource_v2.why: Standard layout (projected gravity + base angular velocity). The runtime loads this via motion_list.yaml, so the vendor's 1 kHz PD loop, fall guard, FSM and damping-on-exit all come for free.

fields.name: motion_ref_pos
fields.note: reference trajectory joint positions, current frame

fields.name: motion_ref_vel
fields.note: reference trajectory joint velocities, current frame

fields.name: ref_gravity
fields.note: gravity in the REFERENCE pelvis frame for the current frame. On the robot it is read from the motion's gravity_guard csv (res/mimic_gravity_guard/<name>.csv: frame_id,gx,gy,gz), and only when that motion has gravity_guard enabled in mimic_opensource_v2_config.yaml CustomConfigs -- otherwise the slot keeps a stale value

fields.name: gvec
fields.note: gravity direction in the robot's base frame, from the IMU quaternion

fields.name: base_ang_vel
fields.note: IMU angular velocity, base frame, x obs_scales.ang_vel

fields.name: joint_pos_err
fields.note: q - default_dof_pos

fields.name: joint_vel
fields.note: raw: the config's obs_scales.dof_vel 0.05 is never applied by the runtime (ReadObservations loads only the ang_vel scale), and the vendor normalizers' std of ~1.5 rad/s confirms unscaled training

fields.name: prev_action
fields.note: raw network output of the previous step

$comment: Reference motion, one .npz per entry in the robot's motion_list.yaml (custom.trajectory_path).
Format read off the robot's own files on 2026-09-19 by decoding the .npy headers inside the zip
(fly_0422.npz T=400, q1_sit T=558, q1_getUp_v3.3 T=309 -- all identical in structure).
This is the mjlab / IsaacLab motion-npz convention, which is further evidence the vendor's
training pipeline is mjlab (their config comments reference sim2sim_mjlab.py).
extra_inputs.n_bodies_note: q1_v3_mc.xml (like q1_v2_mc.xml before it) has nbody=27 including 'world'; 26 == the real bodies, in MJCF body-tree order excluding world (pelvis first). Verified 2026-10-04 against all 16 vendor npz files on the robot: forward kinematics of our q1_v2 MJCF from body 0's pose + joint_pos reproduces body_pos_w to 1e-7 m (the 8 newer files, e.g. getUp v3.1+, lie, lying2Fold) or 7 mm at the ankles (the 8 older ones, made with an earlier shank length). joint_pos is in joints.yaml order; body_quat_w is (w, x, y, z).

mimic_opensource_v2.layout_source: Not the config comment. The comment at the top of mimic_opensource_v2_config.yaml (116 valid + 3 zero padding, gvec at 44, base_w at 47) is stale: the runtime concatenates motion_pos, motion_vel, ref_gravity, gravity, imu_omega, dof_pos, dof_vel, actions (119, nothing padded); the vendor ONNXs' built-in normalizers show the same layout (two gravity-like triples at 44 and 47, angular velocity at 50, real data in 116..118); and the vendor's own policies track in our sim with this layout and fall with the old one. A policy trained on the old layout convulsed and fell on the robot on 2026-10-05.
mimic_opensource_v2.obs_scales_note: the robot config lists dof_vel: 0.05, but the runtime does not apply it (see joint_vel)

walk.why: Velocity-command locomotion that the robot's runtime already runs: replace the ONNX in walk_run.yaml and the vendor's CPG, arm swing, fall guard and FSM come with it. Coupled to the runtime's CPG phase generator, modelled in q1_rl/envs/walk.py (RuntimeCPG).
walk.layout_source: Field order from walk_run.yaml obs_index. Semantics of the fields the config does not spell out (command scaling, pattern, cpg, joint_pos relative or absolute, history order) found on 2026-10-17 by running the vendor's v3.2 policy in our sim under every combination and keeping the one it walks with: commands tracked to 0.04-0.05 m/s RMS over forward / sideways / turn / back / stand, and its own velocity estimator (cv_vel, x2) agrees with the true base velocity to 0.1. With any other pattern, absolute joint angles or a newest-first history it falls within 12 s of the same script; with unscaled commands it walks at 0.0-0.15 m/s when asked for 0.3. tools/check_vendor_walk.py repeats this through Contract.build_obs. NOT yet confirmed against the runtime binary.

fields.name: imu_ang_vel
fields.note: base angular velocity

fields.name: imu_euler
fields.note: roll, pitch only -- NOT a 3-vector projected gravity

fields.name: command
fields.note: vx, vy, wz scaled like legged_gym: (2 vx, 2 vy, wz) -- obs_scales lin_vel / ang_vel. Unscaled, the vendor policy walks at half the speed asked. Its sideways speed tracks better at 3 vy (cmd_y bias 1.5 in walk_run.yaml?), so the runtime may scale vy by more; a policy of ours just walks sideways at a different speed per unit.

fields.name: pattern
fields.note: gait pattern selector; (1, 0) is walking. With (0, 0), (0, 1) or (1, 1) the vendor policy falls in the command script (the other pattern is presumably running).

fields.name: joint_pos_err
fields.note: q - default_dof_pos (walk's), not q: with absolute angles the vendor policy falls

fields.name: prev_action
fields.note: 13 wide: the policy's own action, not the 22 sent to the robot. Verified 2026-10-04 on q1_walkRun_upperPosCtrl v2.1/v3.1/v3.2 (robot software v0.3.0.0.5): the actor outputs 13 (12 legs + waist_roll, by joint order) and the graph concatenates 9 constant zeros to make 22; the other 9 (waist_yaw + 8 arm joints) are position-controlled.

fields.name: cpg
fields.note: (sin 2 pi phi, cos 2 pi phi, -sin 2 pi phi, -cos 2 pi phi): one clock per leg, half a cycle apart. Which leg leads makes no difference to the vendor policy; (cos, sin, ...) and a quarter-cycle offset track worse, all-zero still walks but turns at 0.08 rad/s when asked for 0.6. Cycle time 0.5-0.7 s all work; the runtime picks it (0.25-0.7 s, gait.cycle_time_s) by a law not known yet.

joint_vel_lowpass_hz.$comment: 100 Hz cutoff for all, except two entries at 10 Hz in the vendor's 14-long list

walk.history_order: oldest first, the current frame last (it is also the observations input)

onnx_inputs.$comment: history = 5 x 71; the ONNX also embeds an estimator (base velocity 3, latent 16, terrain 16) fed by the history

velocity.why: Velocity-command walking for the browser viewer's WASD. NOT a layout the robot's runtime knows -- deploying it needs a runtime of our own. Gains, nominal pose and action scale are mimic_opensource_v2's (gains.yaml), so the viewer can switch between this and the tracking policies on the same actuators.

fields.name: command
fields.note: operator command: forward and sideways speed in the heading frame, yaw rate

fields.name: gait
fields.note: sin, cos of the gait clock (period 0.6 s; left foot swings in the first half); (0, 0) when the command is zero

fields.name: gvec
fields.note: gravity direction in the robot's base frame, from the IMU quaternion

fields.name: base_ang_vel
fields.note: IMU angular velocity, base frame

fields.name: joint_pos_err
fields.note: q - default_dof_pos

fields.name: joint_vel
fields.note: raw

fields.name: prev_action
fields.note: raw network output of the previous step
